thread:
maya: quick heads-up — ran a bisect over the AWQ INT8 path after noticing a perf regression on the 4xA100 cluster. baseline (GPTQ) vs AWQ show ~12–18% token latency increase for long-context (1k+) requests when group_size != 128.

jon: curious — is this a kernel fallback or extra copy/packing overhead?

maya: both, unfortunately. profiler shows the kernel chooser is selecting the fast int8-kernel normally, but when group_size is 64 we trigger a different packing routine that serializes KV packing and forces a fallback GEMM path for a handful of layers. snippet from perf log: 
```
layer 12: pack_time=1.72ms (expected 0.46ms)
kernel_selected: int8_gemm_opt  (compat=false)
fallback: generic_gemm  (latency +14%)
```

liam: do we see the same on FP8 or 4-bit?

maya: FP8 path unaffected. 4-bit (gptq-style) has lower packing overhead because it's using a bitpacked loop that avoids the extra per-row memcpy. AWQ's current group packing creates an intermediate aligned buffer which is the culprit.

jon: can you repro with reduced batch size to isolate batching heuristics?

maya: yes — single-request, long sequence still shows the regression. batching reduces relative overhead but doesn't eliminate the per-token penalty for the affected layers.

profiler-bot: flamegraph uploaded: https://internal.s3/redwood/profiler/1749501234/flame.svg

maya: bisect points to two changes: 1) group-size-aware kernel selector tweak (changed compatibility mask) and 2) pack routine refactor (introduced 64-byte alignment step). Reverting either reduces the regression to ~3–4%.

jon: quick mitigation options?

maya: options I tested: 
- force group_size=128 for AWQ models in runtime policy (immediate fix)
- add a fast-path pack for group_size 64 that avoids the extra buffer (safer)
- update kernel chooser to prefer the generic int8 pack-compatible kernel when a pack-refactor flag is enabled (risky for other HW)

liam: what's the perf vs quality tradeoff if we force group_size=128? any eval delta?

maya: did a small eval on our canary prompts — no meaningful quality regression (n=150 prompts). AWQ calibration curve looks flat between 64 and 128 for these models, but that may not hold universally.

jon: sounds reasonable to ship the runtime policy override + quick test harness for wider eval. can you add a canary rollout (25% traffic) and watch token-level latency breakdowns in console?

maya: will do. PR with policy override + unit test for pack path in draft. cc @infra-bot for infra/cluster validation.

infra-bot: noted — will reserve extra GPU capacity for canary and enable detailed tracing for the next 6 hours once PR is merged.

maya: one more note — packing overhead scales with sequence length and KV cache hits. if KV cache is cold, we pay the pack cost once; if hot and we do prefix caching we amortize it. observed worst-case when we had many short-lived sessions with cold KV.

liam: ok let's also add a runtime heuristic: skip the refactored pack buffer on >1 request per connection or when kv_cache_hit_rate > 0.8. should be quick to add.

maya: agree. I'll include that heuristic in the PR and add the perf regression alert rule so Optimize can notify us if median token latency increases >7% for AWQ models.

jon: perfect — thanks. post the PR link when ready and we can promote to canary tonight. :thumbsup:

maya: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4523 (draft)

profiler-bot: test-run summary (1749501372): canary perf delta prefix: +2.8% median token latency when forced-group128, fallback removed: -11.4% on affected model. full logs in CI artifact.

maya: closing loop — will follow up with a short doc on pack implementation and a quick checklist for model onboards to include group_size compatibility notes.
